newsitem.title: USA: Alabama lawmakers propose $125 mln GOs for schools.
newsitem.headline: Alabama lawmakers propose $125 mln GOs for schools.

text.p: An education technology bond bill proposed by Gov. Fob James was formally filed in the Alabama Legislature, but was trimmed by $25 million to $125 million, legislative aides said.

The bill would fund the purchase and installation of computers and internet links at public schools by the end of 1999. It was introduced Tuesday by Rep. Bill Fuller, D-LaFayette and Sen. Hank Sanders, D-Selma.

The plan still calls for $150 million of spending as James proposed in his budget, but the size of the bond issue was reduced because the state will get $23 million of that from federal programs, while other schools have already received computer funding grants from the state legislature.
State School Superintendent Ed Richardson said the proposal would give students in poor school districts the same technological advantages as those in wealthy districts.
He also said the state could absorb the debt service costs on the 12-year bond issue without a tax increase.
